title: Mixed H(div) fluxes, Darcy flow and local conservation

items.title: Contravariant Piola map
items.statement:
Let $\widehat K,K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nondegenerate open simplices and let $F_K:\widehat K\to K$ be the orientation-preserving affine bijection $F_K(\widehat x)=A_K\widehat x+b_K$, where $J_K:=\det A_K>0$. For a measurable vector field $\widehat v$ on $\widehat K$, define its contravariant Piola push-forward by
$$
(\mathcal P_K\widehat v)(x):=J_K^{-1}A_K\widehat v(F_K^{-1}(x)),\qquad x\in K.
$$
The inverse pull-back is $\widehat v(\widehat x)=J_KA_K^{-1}v(F_K(\widehat x))$. Facet normals are oriented consistently with the chosen orientation of $F_K$; the associated oriented surface vector transforms by $n\,ds=J_KA_K^{-T}\widehat n\,d\widehat s$.
items.strategy: State the map, domains, orientation, and inverse convention.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.4, equations (14.8)–(14.12): contravariant Piola mapping and facet flux transformation.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications

items.title: The real H(div) space
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.
items.strategy: Give the typed definition and all conventions; prove claimed well-definedness locally.

items.title: The real zero-mean $L^2$ space is Hilbert
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a measurable set of finite measure, and set
$$L^2_0(D):=\left\{q\in L^2(D;\mathbb R):\int_Dq\,dx=0\right\}.$$
With the real $L^2$ inner product $(q,r)=\int_Dqr\,dx$, $L^2_0(D)$ is a closed real Hilbert subspace of $L^2(D;\mathbb R)$.
items.strategy: Show the integral is a bounded linear functional and its zero set is closed.

items.title: Smooth-neighborhood density in H1 of a simplex
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nondegenerate open simplex. For every $u\in H^1(K;\mathbb R)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a function $u_\varepsilon$ smooth on an open neighborhood of $\overline K$ with $\|u_\varepsilon-u\|_{H^1(K)}<\varepsilon$.
items.strategy: Contract the simplex inward, prove affine-composition continuity in H1, and mollify on the resulting neighborhood.

references.locator: Complete notes, Chapter 3 §3.6 (printed pp. 59–60), smooth approximation of Sobolev functions by mollification.

items.title: Weak normal trace by Green duality
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx
$$
is independent of the representative $w$, defines a bounded real linear functional $\gamma_n v\in T_D'$, and satisfies $\|\gamma_n v\|_{T_D'}\le\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}$. This functional is the weak normal trace; no pointwise boundary value is asserted.
items.strategy: Prove Green independence on the H1_0 closure and bound the quotient functional.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.1.1, Lemma 2.1.1 and its proof: normal trace in the dual trace space and Green's formula.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 16: Local interpolation in H(div) and H(curl) (I)

items.title: Piola divergence and facet-flux identities
items.statement:
Let $F_K(\widehat x)=A_K\widehat x+b_K$ be as in [[def-na-contravariant-piola-map]], and let $\widehat v\in C^1(\overline{\widehat K};\mathbb R^d)$. Set $v=\mathcal P_K\widehat v$. Then
$$
(\operatorname{div}_x v)(F_K(\widehat x))=J_K^{-1}\operatorname{div}_{\widehat x}\widehat v(\widehat x).
$$
For each facet $\widehat F$ mapped to $F$, with the corresponding oriented normals, the integrated flux is preserved:
$$
\int_F v\cdot n_F\,ds=\int_{\widehat F}\widehat v\cdot\widehat n_{\widehat F}\,d\widehat s.
$$
items.strategy: Derive the divergence identity by the affine chain rule and the flux identity by the cofactor surface transformation.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.4, equations (14.8)–(14.12): oriented face transformation and contravariant Piola identities.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.1, equations (2.1.69)–(2.1.74), Piola divergence and normal-flux formulas.

items.title: Zero-normal-trace H(div) space
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev and weak normal trace interfaces. For an open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, let $T_D=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D)$ be the trace quotient of [[lem-na-hdiv-weak-normal-trace]], and let $\gamma_n:H(\operatorname{div};D)\to T_D'$ be its weak normal trace. Define
$$
H_0(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in H(\operatorname{div};D):\gamma_n v=0\text{ in }T_D'\}.
$$
Thus zero normal trace means that the Green-duality functional vanishes on every H1 trace class; no pointwise normal value is required.
items.strategy: Give the typed definition and state exactly which trace is required to vanish.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.1.1, equation (2.1.21), zero-normal-trace subspace of H(div).

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.1 normal-facet flux convention used for the zero-normal finite element subspace.

items.title: Affine simplicial meshes and RT/BDM spaces
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded, connected polyhedral Lipschitz domain. A matching affine simplicial mesh and its shape regularity have the exact meaning of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; additionally, call the mesh facet-connected when its dual graph (one vertex per cell and one edge per shared $(d-1)$-facet) is connected. Write $h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\operatorname{diam}K$.

For $k\ge0$, $\mathbb P_k(K)$ is the real scalar polynomial space of total degree at most $k$, and $\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k$ is the real homogeneous scalar polynomial space of degree exactly $k$ (for $k=0$, the constants). Define
$$\operatorname{RT}_k(K)=\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R^d)+x\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k(K),\qquad \operatorname{BDM}_k(K)=\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R^d)\quad(k\ge1).$$
For either local family $X_k$, its global H(div)-conforming space is
$$X_k(\mathcal T_h)=\{v\in H(\operatorname{div};D):v|_K\in X_k(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T_h\}.
$$
The zero-normal RT0 flux space and mean-zero P0 pressure space are
$$V_h:=\operatorname{RT}_0(\mathcal T_h)\cap H_0(\operatorname{div};D),\qquad Q_h:=\{q\in L^2(D):q|_K\text{ is constant for every }K,\ \int_Dq=0\}.$$
For each mesh facet $F$, fix one unit normal $n_F$; on a cell boundary use the outward unit normal $n_K$, which equals either $n_F$ or $-n_F$. The notation $\mathbb P_0(\mathcal T_h)$ means cellwise constants. No existence of a mesh for every $D$ is asserted by this definition.
items.strategy: Specify the affine map, facet orientation, polynomial families, mesh conformity, shape bound, and the precise global spaces.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §§14.2–14.4: affine simplices, Raviart–Thomas and BDM polynomial spaces, and facet conformity.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.2: affine simplex maps and RT/BDM families.

items.title: Zero mean of the divergence under zero normal trace
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open. If $v\in H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$, then $\operatorname{div}v\in L^1(D)$ and
$$\int_D\operatorname{div}v\,dx=0.$$
items.strategy: Evaluate the Green-duality normal trace on the constant function one.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.1.1, Green formula (2.1.16) and the definition of H0(div).

references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.1 facet-normal flux convention and H(div) boundary interpretation.

items.title: H1-zero fields have zero weak H(div) normal trace
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open. Every real vector field $w\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ belongs to $H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$, where the latter is the kernel of the weak normal trace. In particular, $\operatorname{div}w\in L^2(D)$ and its weak normal trace vanishes on the whole boundary trace quotient.
items.strategy: Approximate by compactly supported smooth fields, use the weak derivative identity against H1 tests, and pass Green duality to the H1 limit.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.1.1: H(div) Green formula and zero-normal boundary subspace.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.1: zero-normal H(div) fluxes and the H1_0 test-space setting.

items.title: H(div) is Hilbert and H0(div) is closed
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For every open $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the real space $H(\operatorname{div};D)$ with the graph inner product
$$
(v,w)_{H(\operatorname{div})}:=(v,w)_{L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)}+(\operatorname{div}v,\operatorname{div}w)_{L^2(D)}
$$
is a Hilbert space. Its subspace $H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$ of [[def-na-h0div-space]] is closed, hence is Hilbert with the restricted inner product.
items.strategy: Use closedness of distributional differentiation for graph completeness and continuity of the weak normal trace for closedness.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.1, equations (2.1.14)–(2.1.16), H(div) graph norm and normal trace continuity.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §§14.1–14.4, H(div) conformity and normal-trace conventions.

items.title: No-flow mixed Darcy problem and coefficient norms
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain, $d\in\{2,3\}$, and set $V:=H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$ and $Q:=L^2_0(D)$ with the real graph and integral inner products from [[def-na-hdiv-space]] and [[lem-na-l2-zero-mean-hilbert]]. A permeability tensor $K(x)$ is a measurable real symmetric $d\times d$ matrix field for which there are constants $0<\kappa_{\min}\le\kappa_{\max}<\infty$ satisfying
$$\kappa_{\min}|\xi|^2\le \xi\cdot K(x)\xi\le\kappa_{\max}|\xi|^2$$
for almost every $x\in D$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb R^d$. It is positive definite almost everywhere, so $K^{-1}$ is measurable and has eigenvalues between $\kappa_{\max}^{-1}$ and $\kappa_{\min}^{-1}$. Define
$$a(u,v):=\int_DK^{-1}u\cdot v,\qquad b(v,q):=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v,$$
and the weighted flux norm $\|v\|_{K^{-1}}:=a(v,v)^{1/2}$. For data $F\in V'$ and $f\in Q$, the no-flow mixed Darcy problem is to find $(u,p)\in V\times Q$ such that
$$a(u,v)+b(v,p)=F(v)\quad(v\in V),\qquad b(u,q)=-\int_D f q\quad(q\in Q).$$
The pressure space's zero-mean constraint fixes the additive constant (Neumann) gauge; $u\in H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$ encodes zero weak normal flux on the full boundary. In the standard source-only Darcy problem used for hybridization, $F=0$.
items.strategy: Specify all coefficient, source, space, sign, boundary, gauge, and weighted-norm conventions.

references.locator: Complete book, Lesson 9 §1.1, pp. 152–155: mixed Darcy formulation and flux-pressure signs.

items.title: Cell averaging is the $L^2$ projection onto P0
items.statement:
For a finite conforming simplicial mesh of bounded $D$, define $P_0:L^2(D)\to\mathbb P_0(\mathcal T_h)$ cellwise by
$$ (P_0g)|_K=|K|^{-1}\int_Kg. $$
Then $P_0$ is linear, equals the identity on piecewise constants, is the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto that space, satisfies $\|P_0g\|_2\le\|g\|_2$, and preserves the integral $\int_DP_0g=\int_Dg$.
items.strategy: Prove orthogonality by cellwise integration, then use Cauchy–Schwarz for contraction and sum cell integrals.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.1: piecewise-constant cell projections used with RT divergence.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2: finite-dimensional $L^2$ projections and piecewise-constant spaces.

items.title: Piola maps RT and BDM polynomial families onto the physical cell
items.statement:
For any $d\ge1$, write $\mathbb P_k$ for real scalar polynomials of total degree at most $k$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k$ for homogeneous scalar polynomials of degree $k$, including zero, and define the local families $\operatorname{RT}_k=\mathbb P_k^d+x\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k$ and $\operatorname{BDM}_k=\mathbb P_k^d$.

Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an orientation-preserving affine bijection between nondegenerate $d$-simplices, with $J=\det A>0$, and use the contravariant Piola map of [[def-na-contravariant-piola-map]]. For every $k\ge0$, it maps $\operatorname{RT}_k(\widehat K)$ bijectively onto $\operatorname{RT}_k(K)$, and for every $k\ge1$ it maps $\operatorname{BDM}_k(\widehat K)$ bijectively onto $\operatorname{BDM}_k(K)$.
items.strategy: Expand the affine push-forward polynomial and split its scalar factor into its degree-k homogeneous part and lower-degree remainder; apply the same argument to the inverse map.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.4: affine contravariant Piola map preserves RT and BDM spaces.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.2, affine transformation formulas for RT and BDM elements.

items.title: The RT0/P0 discrete kernel is exactly divergence-free
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the mesh conventions of [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. With $V_h=\operatorname{RT}_0(\mathcal T_h)\cap H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$, $Q_h=\mathbb P_0(\mathcal T_h)\cap L^2_0(D)$ and $b(v_h,q_h)=-\int_Dq_h\operatorname{div}v_h$, the discrete kernel
$$Z_h:=\{v_h\in V_h:b(v_h,q_h)=0\text{ for every }q_h\in Q_h\}$$
is exactly $\{v_h\in V_h:\operatorname{div}v_h=0\}$.
items.strategy: Use div(V_h) subset Q_h and test the orthogonality with div(v_h) itself.

references.locator: Complete chapter, §§14.1–14.2: H(div)-conforming RT fields and piecewise-constant divergence.

items.title: H1 facet trace inequality on shape-regular simplices
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For a nondegenerate affine simplex $K$ with diameter $h_K$ and shape bound $h_K/r_K\le\gamma$, and any facet $F$, every $u\in H^1(K)$ has a well-defined trace $\gamma_Fu\in L^2(F)$ and
$$
\|\gamma_Fu\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C(d,\gamma)\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|u\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(K)}^2\bigr).
$$
items.strategy: Prove the reference-simplex face estimate along inward segments for smooth functions, then extend by the local density lemma and scale by the affine map.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 16: Local interpolation in H(div) and H(curl) (I)
references.locator: Complete chapter, §16.1.1: Sobolev trace and the regularity domain of facet moments.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §2.1: normal traces and integration by parts on Lipschitz cells.

items.title: Hybridized no-flow RT0/P0 Darcy system
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

Assume the no-flow Darcy data of [[def-na-neumann-darcy-mixed-problem]] and a facet-connected conforming mesh from [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. Let $\mathcal F_h^i$ be its interior facets. On each cell $K$, let
$$W_K:=\{v\in\operatorname{RT}_0(K):v\cdot n_K=0\text{ on every boundary facet of }D\text{ contained in }\partial K\}.$$
The broken flux space is $W_h:=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T_h}W_K$, the cell pressure space is $M_h:=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\mathbb R$, and the skeleton multiplier space is $\Lambda_h:=\prod_{F\in\mathcal F_h^i}\mathbb R$. The scalar $\lambda_F$ is constant on facet $F$ and uses the fixed orientation only to label that facet; local equations use the outward normal of each cell.

For the source-only problem $F=0$, a hybrid solution $(u_h,p_h,\lambda_h)\in W_h\times M_h\times\Lambda_h$ for $f\in Q$ satisfies, for every cell $K$, every $v_K\in W_K$, and every interior facet $F=K^+\cap K^-$,
$$\int_KK^{-1}u_K\cdot v_K-\int_Kp_K\operatorname{div}v_K+\sum_{F\subset\partial K,\ F\in\mathcal F_h^i}\lambda_F\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K=0,$$
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}u_K=\int_Kf,$$
$$\int_F(u_{K^+}\cdot n_{K^+}+u_{K^-}\cdot n_{K^-})=0.$$
Because each RT0 normal component is constant on a facet, the last equation is pointwise normal-flux matching. With physical-boundary flux zero, the transformation $p_K\mapsto p_K+c$ for all cells and $\lambda_F\mapsto\lambda_F+c$ leaves the hybrid equations unchanged: in the local first equation the change is $-c\int_K\operatorname{div}v_K+c\sum_{F\text{ interior}}\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K=0$ by Gauss–Green and the zero physical-boundary flux; the mass and jump equations do not use pressure or multipliers. This is the common pressure gauge.
items.strategy: State the local and skeleton unknowns, all signs/orientations, and the gauge transformation explicitly.

items.title: H1 traces agree across interior mesh facets
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a polyhedral open set with a conforming affine simplicial mesh, let $K_+$ and $K_-$ share an interior facet $F$, and let $w\in H^1(D)$. The elementwise $L^2(F)$ traces of $w|_{K_+}$ and $w|_{K_-}$ agree almost everywhere on $F$.
items.strategy: Localize around compact subfacets, mollify the single H1 field across the interface, and use the simplex trace bound to pass equality of smooth traces to the elementwise traces.

references.locator: Complete chapter, §16.1.1, trace spaces and elementwise facet moments.

references.locator: Complete notes, Chapter 3 §§3.2–3.4: cutoff localization, mollification and Sobolev approximation.

items.title: RT0 facet-flux unisolvence and global H(div) conformity
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the mesh conventions of [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. On each $d$-simplex $K$, $\operatorname{RT}_0(K)=\{a+cx:a\in\mathbb R^d,c\in\mathbb R\}$ has dimension $d+1$, and the $d+1$ integrated outward facet-normal fluxes determine its element uniquely. A piecewise RT0 field belongs to $H(\operatorname{div};D)$ exactly when its oriented integrated fluxes match across every shared facet; such a field belongs to $H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$ exactly when its normal component (equivalently its integrated outward flux) also vanishes on every boundary facet.
items.strategy: Prove local unisolvence, cancel interior distributional fluxes, and use the trace agreement lemma to identify the weak external normal trace.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §14.1, printed pp. 156–157: RT0 unisolvence, facet flux degrees of freedom and global conformity.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §§2.2–2.3: RT degrees of freedom and conformity.

items.title: Continuous mixed Darcy well-posedness with pressure gauge
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses in [[def-na-neumann-darcy-mixed-problem]] on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain in dimension two or three. For every $F\in V'$ and $f\in Q$, there is a unique $(u,p)\in V\times Q$ solving
$$a(u,v)+b(v,p)=F(v),\qquad b(u,q)=-\int_Dfq$$
for all $v\in V,q\in Q$. The graph norm on the flux and zero-mean pressure norm make these equations well-posed; the mean-zero pressure convention fixes the Neumann gauge.
items.strategy: Verify boundedness, continuous inf-sup from the actual divergence right inverse, and coercivity on the divergence-free kernel, then apply the supplier Babuška–Brezzi theorem.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part XI Chapter 49: Well-posedness for PDEs in mixed form

items.title: Canonical RT0 interpolation on H1 fields
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, a conforming affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ from [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]], and $v\in H^1(D;\mathbb R^d)$. The facet trace inequality of [[lem-na-simplex-h1-facet-trace-bound]] makes each moment $m_F(v):=\int_F\gamma_Fv\cdot n_F$ finite. On each cell $K$, use its outward normals to prescribe the $d+1$ facet moments (with sign reversed when $n_F$ points inward to $K$); by RT0 flux unisolvence in [[lem-na-rt0-unisolvence-and-global-conformity]], there is a unique $I_Kv\in\operatorname{RT}_0(K)$ with those moments. Define $I_hv$ by $(I_hv)|_K=I_Kv$. The elementwise traces of the global H1 field agree almost everywhere across each shared facet by [[lem-na-h1-interior-facet-traces-agree]], so the shared moment is single-valued in the fixed orientation; the same unisolvence result gives $I_hv\in\operatorname{RT}_0(\mathcal T_h)\subset H(\operatorname{div};D)$. No canonical facet-moment definition on rough H(div)-only input is made here.
items.strategy: Specify the input regularity, facet moments, orientation, and elementwise outputs.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 16: Local interpolation in H(div) and H(curl) (I)
references.locator: Complete chapter, §16.1: canonical RT interpolation defined by facet flux moments on H1 fields.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications

items.title: Exact RT0/P0 element mass balance and normal continuity
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, the mesh conventions of [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]], and let $(u_h,p_h)\in V_h\times Q_h$ solve the discrete Darcy equations with source $f\in L^2_0(D)$. Then on every cell $K$,
$$\operatorname{div}u_h|_K=|K|^{-1}\int_Kf,\qquad\int_K\operatorname{div}u_h=\int_Kf.$$
The normal flux is single-valued on every interior facet and zero on every boundary facet.
items.strategy: Use orthogonality to all mean-zero piecewise constants, total compatibility, and the global RT0 normal degrees of freedom.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 14: H(div) finite elements
references.locator: Complete chapter, §§14.1–14.2: RT normal continuity and cellwise divergence.

references.title: Francisco-Javier Sayas, A gentle introduction to the Finite Element Method (2015)

items.title: Boundedness and divergence commutation of RT0 interpolation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, a shape-regular mesh with $h=\max_Kh_K$, and $I_h$ from [[def-na-rt0-h1-interpolation]]. There is $C$ depending only on dimension and the shape bound such that every $v\in H^1(D;\mathbb R^d)$ satisfies
$$\|I_hv\|_{L^2(D)}\le C(\|v\|_{L^2(D)}+h\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}),\qquad (\operatorname{div}I_hv)|_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K\operatorname{div}v.$$
If $v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, then $I_hv\in V_h$.
items.strategy: Use explicit RT0 facet basis functions and trace scaling; prove commutation by the divergence theorem and constant divergence.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 16: Local interpolation in H(div) and H(curl) (I)
references.locator: Complete chapter, §§16.1.1–16.1.2: RT interpolation stability and its divergence-commuting relation.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications
references.locator: Complete textbook, Chapter 2 §§2.2–2.3: interpolation estimates and commuting diagram.

items.title: Uniform RT0/P0 divergence lift and inf-sup bound
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral $D$ in dimension two or three, and a shape-regular conforming mesh. Let $C_I$ be the mesh-independent constant in the RT0 interpolation estimate and let $L$ be a coordinate-slab width for $D$. If $B_D$ is the actual right inverse of [[thm-na-bounded-lipschitz-domain-divergence-right-inverse]], define
$$S_hq_h:=I_hB_Dq_h,\qquad C_R:=C_I C_{\rm div}(L+\operatorname{diam}D).$$
Then $S_h:Q_h\to V_h$ is a linear right inverse of divergence and $\|S_hq_h\|_{L^2(D)}\le C_R\|q_h\|_{L^2(D)}$. Consequently $\|S_hq_h\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le\sqrt{1+C_R^2}\|q_h\|_2$. When $Q_h\ne\{0\}$, the RT0/P0 inf-sup constant satisfies $\beta_h\ge(1+C_R^2)^{-1/2}$ uniformly in mesh size.
items.strategy: Compose the actual H1 divergence lift with the H1-domain RT0 interpolant and derive the graph-norm and inf-sup constants.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part III Chapter 16: Local interpolation in H(div) and H(curl) (I)
references.locator: Complete chapter, §16.1: divergence-commuting RT interpolation and stable facet moments.

references.title: Daniele Boffi, Franco Brezzi and Michel Fortin, Mixed Finite Element Methods and Applications

items.title: Bounded commuting projection onto the zero-normal RT0 space
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and a shape-regular mesh. Let $P_0$ be the cellwise $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto piecewise constants, let $S_h:Q_h\to V_h$ be the stable right inverse above, and put $Z_h=\{z_h\in V_h:\operatorname{div}z_h=0\}$. There is a linear projection $\Pi_h:H_0(\operatorname{div};D)\to V_h$ such that
$$\operatorname{div}\Pi_hv=P_0\operatorname{div}v,\qquad \|\Pi_hv\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le C\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div})},$$
where $C$ depends on the domain and mesh shape bound, not mesh size. The construction uses the finite-dimensional $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto $Z_h$ and never applies facet moments to rough H(div)-only fields.
items.strategy: Decompose into a stable discrete divergence lift and the L2 projection onto the discrete kernel; verify commutation, identity on V_h, and the uniform graph-norm bound.

references.locator: Complete chapter, §§16.1–16.2: bounded commuting projections and the limits of canonical facet interpolation.

items.title: RT0/P0 Darcy stability and flux/pressure error bound
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, the Darcy data in [[def-na-neumann-darcy-mixed-problem]], and a facet-connected shape-regular mesh. For at least two cells, set $C_R$ as in the stable lift theorem and define
$$\widehat\beta=(1+C_R^2)^{-1/2},\quad M_a=\kappa_{\min}^{-1},\quad M_b=1,\quad\alpha_*=\kappa_{\max}^{-1}.$$
Let $(u,p)$ solve the continuous source-only Darcy problem ($F=0$) and $(u_h,p_h)$ the RT0/P0 Galerkin system. For any $w_h\in V_h,r_h\in Q_h$, put $\delta_u=\|u-w_h\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}$, $\delta_p=\|p-r_h\|_2$, and
$$R_h=\widehat\beta^{-1}M_b\delta_u,$$
$$U_h=\delta_u+\alpha_*^{-1}\{M_a(\delta_u+R_h)+M_b\delta_p\}+R_h,$$
$$P_h=\delta_p+\widehat\beta^{-1}\{M_a(U_h+\delta_u)+M_b\delta_p\}.$$
Then the discrete pair exists uniquely and
$$\|u-u_h\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le U_h,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_2\le P_h,\qquad \|u-u_h\|_{K^{-1}}\le\kappa_{\min}^{-1/2}U_h.$$
For a one-cell mesh $V_h=Q_h=\{0\}$, so the unique discrete pair is $(0,0)$; the nonzero-$Q_h$ error theorem is not invoked. The constants display permeability contrast and do not assert contrast-independent robustness.
items.strategy: Separate the zero-space one-cell case; otherwise verify the discrete bounds and kernel coercivity, apply the actual beta_h-sensitive mixed Galerkin theorem, and state every coefficient-dependent constant.

items.title: Hybridization, static condensation, and pressure gauge
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the source-only Darcy system and hybrid equations of [[def-na-hybridized-rt0-darcy-system]] on a facet-connected mesh. The hybrid solutions modulo the common pressure shift $(p,\lambda)\mapsto(p+c,\lambda+c)$ are in one-to-one correspondence with the conforming RT0/P0 Darcy solution. If the mesh has at least two cells, every local flux-pressure saddle block is invertible; eliminating these local variables gives a linear system on the interior-facet multipliers whose nullspace is exactly the one-dimensional constant gauge. For one cell, the conforming flux and mean-zero pressure spaces are zero and the hybrid pressure is entirely gauge.
items.strategy: Prove both directions using the broken-to-conforming jump map, characterize its annihilator, verify local saddle-block invertibility, and identify the sole gauge mode.

title: Mixed H(div) fluxes, Darcy flow and local conservation — Examples

items.title: A continuous P1 pressure gives a nonconservative primal flux
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

On the unit square split along the diagonal from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$, the continuous piecewise-affine pressure with nodal values $0,0,1,0$ at $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ has negative gradient $q=(0,-1)$ below the diagonal and $q=(-1,0)$ above it. Each cellwise divergence is zero, but the normal flux jumps by magnitude $\sqrt2$ across the diagonal; hence this piecewise field is not in $H(\operatorname{div};D)$ and does not have a locally conservative global flux.
items.strategy: Compute both affine gradients, the oriented diagonal normal components, and the resulting distributional interface divergence.

items.title: A constant Darcy flux on the reference triangle
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

On $K=\{(x,y):x>0,y>0,x+y<1\}$ with unit permeability, $q=(1,0)$ and $p=-x$ satisfy $q+\nabla p=0$ and $\operatorname{div}q=0$. Their outward integrated facet fluxes on $x=0$, $y=0$, and $x+y=1$ are respectively $-1,0,+1$, so exact local mass balance holds.
items.strategy: Verify the pointwise Darcy equations and calculate each facet flux with its outward unit normal.

items.title: Checkerboard permeability and the explicit contrast factor
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

On a $2\times2$ checkerboard of equal squares, split each square into two affine triangles and set scalar permeability $K=1$ on one color and $K=10^6$ on the other. Then $\kappa_{\min}=1$, $\kappa_{\max}=10^6$, the weighted energy assigns coefficients $1$ and $10^{-6}$ to the two regions, and the RT0/P0 graph-norm error constants include $\alpha_*^{-1}=10^6$ and $M_a/\alpha_*=10^6$.
items.strategy: Evaluate the coefficient bounds cell by cell and substitute them into the theorem's explicit constants.

items.title: Two-triangle hybrid RT0 local elimination
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

Split the unit square by its diagonal into $K_1=\{0<y<x<1\}$ and $K_2=\{0<x<y<1\}$. For unit permeability and $f=1$ on $K_1$, $f=-1$ on $K_2$, the hybrid solution has
$$u_1=\tfrac12\theta_1,\quad u_2=-\tfrac12\theta_2,\quad p_1=\tfrac1{12},\quad p_2=-\tfrac1{12},\quad\lambda=0,$$
where $\theta_1(x,y)=(x-1,y)$ and $\theta_2(x,y)=(x,y-1)$. The local elimination equations reduce to $t_K/6-p_K+\lambda=0$, $t_1=1/2$, $t_2=-1/2$, and $t_1+t_2=0$; changing $\lambda$ shifts both pressures by the same constant and is precisely the gauge.
items.strategy: Use the unit-facet-flux RT0 basis on each triangle to solve the finite hybrid equations exactly.
